correctness.rationale: The explicit modal-depth-one support tests give a bijection between all single-agent S5 formula equivalence classes and anti-extensive set maps. The product sample space produces independent uniform per-support choices. Each nonempty fixed support is a Bernoulli event, giving the generating function and universal-extinction product. Induction on support size proves the exact half-extinction law for any specified initial support. Expanding logarithms yields the stated asymptotic with a uniform tail estimate. Checker.py exhaustively verifies 2+16+4096 small maps and modal support realizations on representative samples; symbolic reasoning, not finite experiments, proves all quantifiers.

value.rationale: The quantitative gap between extinction of one chosen epistemic information cell and extinction of every possible cell is a naturally motivated invariant of repeated information updates. The exact one-half law independent of support size contrasts with a product rare-event law whose logarithm grows on the (3/2)^m scale, and the explicit fixed-support PGF gives a complete finite distribution for all vocabularies. This is meaningful structure and a complete natural census, not an arbitrary tiny parameter increment.
